notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to open the source pages was blocked because the web tool had no calls left, so I didn't read any commentary on Psalm 64.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I read nothing, I have no notes to give you. Writing from memory would break that rule, so I haven't.

**What I was going to read** (please check these addresses; I haven't confirmed they all exist):
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-64/
- Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub: biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/64.htm (and the same with /ellicott/ and /pulpit/ in place of /gill/)
- Precept Austin's Psalm 64 page
- The NET Bible notes on Psalm 64 at netbible.org
- Augustine's sermons on the Psalms at newadvent.org. His Latin Bible numbers this psalm 63, so his "Psalm 64" is a different psalm.
- Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on Psalm 64 (spurgeon.org or ccel.org), for a Baptist reading
- After those, searches for the other traditions: Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, and Lutheran, Pentecostal and Orthodox sites

**Next steps:** If you send this request again in a new turn, I'll start over with this list and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point. If you'd like, you could also paste in the text of any of these pages, and I'll write the notes from that.
